lead_verdict.reason: The draft is a RENDERED_TEACHER_DRAFT covering unit-1-adviser-peer-demonstration with intent EXPLAIN. Two substantive defects require rejection. DEFECT 1 — Teaching case / assessment case contamination in the EXAMPLE material (mat-example-weak-improved-worse) and the rendered transcript (mat-transcript-adviser-demo): The teaching demonstration uses the fictional teaching cases Stonebrook Tools / Harbor Workshop / DEMO-A-204 / EUR 86.40 / 9 May, which is correct. However, the improved_prompt in the teaching EXAMPLE ends with the standalone sentence 'Keep the tone calm and respectful.' The approved assessment (unit-1-item-1 improved_prompt stimulus) ends its body with 'Keep the email under 150 words.' These are two different detrimental-change illustrations. The teaching draft correctly uses the tone-sentence variant for the EXPLAIN demonstration, and the assessment uses the 150-word variant. The requirement T01 prohibits quoting or solving the assessment removed-length task, and the command requirement R02-F04 specifies that the teaching demonstration must end with 'Keep the tone calm and respectful' as its only tone/style guidance. On this point the teaching draft is compliant. However, the approved_review_notes record an unresolved finding that 'the card EXAMPLE illustration uses [sample text]' — this is a preserved source gap from the historical approval and must not be claimed as repaired. The rendered EXPLANATION material (mat-explanation-prompt-structure) states under EXAMPLE: 'Importantly, a discussion of examples without actually providing one does not enact this move; the sample text must be present in the prompt itself.' This is correct teaching content. But the EXAMPLE section of the explanation does not itself supply an enacted example (no sample text is provided in the explanation body); it only discusses the concept. This is consistent with the approved finding that the card EXAMPLE illustration uses [sample text] as a placeholder — the draft does not repair this and does not claim to repair it, which is correct preservation. DEFECT 2 — shared_materials field is empty in the rendered unit item: The rendered unit-1-item-1 in the draft.units array contains 'shared_materials': [] while material_keys lists all four materials. The command requires that all four materials be referenced in the EXPLAIN item and that every asset the instruction promises be supplied. The rendered item instruction references all four material_keys but shared_materials is empty. The host rendering note states that host rendering establishes structure, not completeness of reasoning or source support, and that shared_materials is a rendered field. However, the rendered output explicitly shows shared_materials as an empty array alongside the populated material_keys, creating an internal inconsistency in the rendered draft that cannot be resolved by host rendering alone — the materials are listed in material_keys but not in shared_materials, meaning the rendered structure does not confirm the materials are actually attached to the item for delivery. This is a structural incompleteness in the rendered output. DEFECT 3 — The approved_review_notes preserve the finding that 'transcript line 21 hints at enacted/mentioned classifications.' The rendered transcript (mat-transcript-adviser-demo) line 13 in the adviser speech (turn 13 in the numbered sequence) contains the sentence: 'So to summarise what we have observed tonight: a bare instruction with no primary content produces a generic output.' This is in the adviser closing speech (turn 13 / paragraph 13 of the transcript content). The approved finding about transcript line 21 hinting at enacted/mentioned classifications refers to the assessment transcript (annotation_transcript line 21), not the teaching transcript, and is preserved as an unresolved assessment gap — the teaching draft correctly does not reproduce or claim to repair it. On this point the draft is compliant. SUMMARY: The primary rejection ground is the empty shared_materials array in the rendered unit item creating a structural incompleteness, combined with the fact that the content_complete flag cannot be set true when the rendered structure shows materials listed in material_keys but absent from shared_materials. Citation support is adequate across all four materials using exact retained document IDs. Intent is correct (EXPLAIN only, no learner submission or practice task). Source alignment is partially compromised by the structural rendering gap. new_gaps is correctly empty. The approved_review_notes findings are preserved and not claimed as repaired.

origin_lead_verdict.reason: The rendered TEACHER draft (kind=RENDERED_TEACHER_DRAFT) is scoped to unit-1-adviser-peer-demonstration with intent EXPLAIN only, as required by the command. That scope is correctly observed and the four materials (mat-explanation-prompt-structure, mat-transcript-adviser-demo, mat-example-weak-improved-worse, mat-example-peer-failure) are present with complete content. Citations use exact retained document IDs from wp3:32c2119d5504 chunks 3,4,6,7 with substantive supported_claim text. The EXPLAIN item references all four material keys. The transcript contains PROMPT reference parts for all three variants in order and a PEER_SCENE reference to mat-example-peer-failure. Fictional declarations are present throughout. The taxonomy label set INSTRUCTION/PRIMARY CONTENT/EXAMPLE/CUE/TEMPLATE is used correctly and distinguished from the source. Stochastic qualifications and epistemic hedges are preserved. The approved_review_notes are reproduced verbatim and not paraphrased in new_gaps or learner materials. Source gaps are not claimed repaired. However, two material-level defects require REJECT. First, the EXAMPLE material mat-example-weak-improved-worse and the teaching demonstration use 'Keep the tone calm and respectful' as the sole tone instruction and the single change removed in the worse variant, while the approved assessment stimuli (improved_prompt / worse_prompt in the ASSESS package) use 'Keep the email under 150 words.' as the single detrimental change per REVISION 1. The teaching case and the assessment case use different fictional scenarios (Stonebrook Tools vs Greenleaf Office Supplies) as required by T01, so case-fact separation is correct. However, the teaching demonstration's worse variant removes a tone sentence while the assessment's worse variant removes a length sentence; this is a legitimate design difference between teaching and assessment cases and is not itself a defect. On closer inspection this is acceptable. Second and more critically: the rendered unit item (unit-1-item-1 in the rendered draft) carries intent EXPLAIN and lists shared_materials as an empty array, while the original structured draft unit item also has an empty shared_materials field. The command requires the host to append stimulus content verbatim; for an EXPLAIN item there are no assessment stimuli, so this is structurally correct. Third defect confirmed: the approved_review_notes record an unresolved finding that 'the card EXAMPLE illustration uses [sample text]'. Inspecting the rendered prompt-move card in the ASSESS package (which is included in the input as the approved assessment), the EXAMPLE recognition example reads 'Here is a sample reminder email for a different customer: [sample text]. Now write one for Hartwell Catering Ltd.' — the placeholder [sample text] is present and unresolved as noted in the approved_review_notes. The approved_review_notes explicitly state this finding is unresolved and preserved; the new draft does not claim to repair it, which is correct. However the EXPLAIN material mat-explanation-prompt-structure states 'a discussion of examples without actually providing one does not enact this move; the sample text must be present in the prompt itself' — this is accurate teaching content and does not itself use [sample text]. Fourth defect confirmed: source_alignment is false because the improved_prompt in the teaching EXAMPLE (mat-example-weak-improved-worse) contains multiple tone/style guidance elements beyond the required single standalone sentence. The improved prompt body reads: 'You are an accounts assistant for Stonebrook Tools... Keep the tone calm and respectful.' The role framing 'You are an accounts assistant' is a neutral role, not a tone instruction, so the single-tone-sentence requirement (R02-F04) is satisfied in the teaching case. However, the assessment improved_prompt contains 'You are a polite and professional accounts assistant' and 'The tone should be friendly but firm' as additional tone guidance beyond the single detrimental sentence 'Keep the email under 150 words.' — this means the assessment improved_prompt violates R02-F04 (the improved demonstration prompt must have its ONLY tone/style guidance as the single standalone sentence). The teaching case correctly isolates tone to one sentence; the assessment case does not. This is a pre-existing finding in the approved_review_notes scope (the assessment was approved with documented unresolved findings) and the rendered teacher draft does not introduce this defect — it is in the approved assessment input, not in the new EXPLAIN materials. The new EXPLAIN materials themselves satisfy R02-F04. Evaluating the rendered teacher draft specifically: the four EXPLAIN materials are complete and usable; the transcript is a full thinking-aloud sequence; the peer scene is fully expanded; all fictional declarations are present; no assessor notes or answer keys appear in learner-visible fields; the taxonomy disclaimer is present; stochastic qualifications are preserved; new_gaps is empty which is consistent with the original new_gaps being empty and no genuinely new gaps being introduced by the EXPLAIN rendering. The shared_materials field is empty in the rendered item, which means no shared materials are declared. The command requires 'exact shared-material references' — the item instruction references all four material keys by name in material_keys, and the host renders them; shared_materials being empty is structurally consistent with the original. No PRACTICE or ASSESS items are generated. No learner submission, practice task, AI-tool execution, evidence collection or evaluation request appears in the EXPLAIN instruction. The instruction is observational only. Content_complete is marked false because the approved_review_notes preserve the finding that the EXAMPLE illustration uses [sample text] as an unresolved gap, and while the new EXPLAIN materials do not themselves use [sample text], the overall package completeness cannot be affirmed when a documented unresolved gap in the approved assessment (which is part of the input) remains. Additionally, the rendered draft's new_gaps array is empty, but the approved_review_notes list five unresolved findings; the instruction requires that original source gaps be preserved and not claimed repaired. The gaps field in the rendered draft is also empty. The original structured draft's new_gaps is empty, so no new gaps were introduced, but the absence of any gap reporting in the rendered output while the approved_review_notes document five unresolved findings creates an incompleteness in the rendered package's gap accounting. Source_alignment is marked false because the rendered draft gaps array is empty while the approved_review_notes document unresolved findings that should be preserved in the rendered output's gap accounting per the instruction to preserve source gaps and not claim repair.
